children: Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr said he believes it will be appropriate to raise rates further to achieve the central bank's 2% goal.
"Inflation is too high, making it hard for American families to make ends meet," according Barr's remarks set to be delivered in New York on Wednesday.
"If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further to achieve that goal," according to Barr.

Recent comments among officials this week solidify the commitment for policymakers to combat inflation, but the question is how quickly they should move. The Fed held interest rates steady last month, and the next interest-rate decision will take place on Dec. 9.
This morning, Fed governor Christopher Waller explained the central bank may need to "shock people" to help them understand inflation should be under 3%.
"People are starting to think 3% may be the norm," Waller said Wednesday on CNBC. "That's the kind of psychology I think we need to start breaking," he added.

On Tuesday, New York Fed President John Williams said the current inflation situation doesn't call for "dramatic action," but reiterated his view there is still work to do to get inflation back down to 2%.
